The final dataset consists of a pilot corpus with 100 tweets per language and comparable corpora of 5,647 English tweets, 4,014 French tweets, and 3,353 Arabic tweets [6].

They obtained part-of-speech tags by leveraging basic natural language processing modules such as tokenization and part-of-speech tagging [2].
The paper compares to the +global-deep context model and other baselines such as the Transformer (base/big) model [3].

The paper defines "complexity" and "confusability" of entity mentions as characteristics that make entity recognition challenging, such as being multi-token, emerging, or having ambiguous forms that require a deep understanding of context to accurately identify and disambiguate [5].
The dataset contains over 29% offensive content, indicating it is not balanced [2].

Yes, they test against the large version of RoBERTa [5].
The length constraints they set were translations longer than 0.25 times the source sentence length [3].

summary.text: The Bengals – Browns rivalry, often referred to as the Battle of Ohio, is a rivalry between the Cincinnati Bengals and Cleveland Browns of the National Football League (NFL).
